elements.element: Vendor duty to defend Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim"

elements.element: Indemnity covers allegation that services/deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: "an allegation that the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any deliverable furnished by TrueLink infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Indemnity covers Vendor's breach of law
Indemnity covers data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content caused by TrueLink"

elements.element: Indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence / wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "(iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct"
"Client shall give TrueLink prompt written notice of the claim"

elements.element: Standard procedure: Vendor control of defence
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall control the defense of the claim"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content
elements.evidence: "Client's indemnity under this Section 12.a is limited to claims arising out of Client Content"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: "and claims arising out of any violation by Client of any state or federal law, rule or regulation"

elements.element: Fallback: IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications)
elements.evidence: No exclusions appear; new clause c contains only "to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Hosting Services...infringes"
No procure/modify/replace/refund language anywhere in clause c.

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No cap or super-cap language inserted.

reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are present in the inserted clause c: defend-and-indemnify running to Client and affiliates, third-party IP infringement of the Hosting Services, Support Services and deliverables, breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with notice, Vendor control and Customer cooperation.

The second insertion supplies the preferred limitation on Customer's indemnity, expressly narrowing Section 12.a to Client Content and Client's violation of state or federal law, matching the two permitted heads.

The fallback bargain (usual exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, 3× annual fees super-cap) is not satisfied, but the locked target is preferred, which is met, so this is not a deficiency.

Minimality holds: two concise insertions were used — a new indemnity where none existed and a one-sentence limiter — with no hold-harmless language, no extra indemnitees, no Customer defence duty, no settlement mechanics beyond notice/control/cooperation, and no rewrite of untouched 12.a or 12.b.

Intent is preserved: TrueLink's existing breach indemnity at 12.b remains effective, the limiter uses the defined term Client Content and cites the existing Section 12.a, and no undefined term, contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced.
